auditor: Claude Fable 5 — independent hostile follow-up audit
target: HWA release candidate, HyperEVM mainnet chain 999, Project X V3
trustPosture: No previous report, closure note or gate result accepted as evidence. Every property re-derived from source and, where possible, executed.

findings.title: The FWA core to FWARewardsHyperEVM boundary is executed by no test in the repository, so rewards solvency was entirely unproven at the release gate
findings.lines: FWARewardsHyperEVM.t.sol:46 (CORE = address(0xF0A)); invariant suites: zero rewards references
findings.scenario: The release gate presents 136 passing Solidity tests and three stateful invariants as proof of custody and liability conservation. None of that evidence covers the configuration mainnet actually runs. `FWA.setRewards` is called by zero test files; it appears only in deployment scripts. Both stateful campaigns construct an FWA whose `rewards` is the zero address, so `_finishAcquisition` takes the `address(r) == 0` branch and never calls `settleAcquisition` or `refundAcquisition`. `FWARewardsHyperEVM.t.sol` impersonates the core with the EOA constant `address(0xF0A)`, so the module is never driven by real core sequencing. Meanwhile `DeployHyperEVMMainnetCore` latches `REWARDS_REQUIRED_FOR_ACTIVATION` one-way, which makes a bound rewards module mandatory on chain 999: acquisitions cannot open without it.
findings.preconditions: None. This is the shipped state of the test suite.
findings.impact: Every reward hook reachable only through the core — registerAcquisition, settleAcquisition, refundAcquisition, startEmission and buyFor — was unexecuted. A double-settle, a missed terminal hook desynchronising `pendingAcquisitionsInEpoch`, an escrow slice booked without funding, or any HYPE/HWA conservation break at that boundary would have passed the gate silently. This is false assurance on the same class of claim as the previous round's F5-001, in the adjacent subsystem.
findings.evidence: Select-String for 'setRewards' across test/, fork-test/ and hyperevm-fork-test/ returns no matches; the same search across script/ returns BindNestRewards.s.sol:67, BindProjectXRewards.s.sol:59 and DeployHyperSwapModules.s.sol:100. Grep for 'rewards' in the three invariant/branch suites returns 0 occurrences each.
findings.fix: Two additive test files. `test/FWARewardsIntegrationInvariant.t.sol` wires a real FWARewardsHyperEVM into a real FWA via setRewards and runs a two-actor, 14-selector stateful campaign (256 runs x 64 depth, 0 reverts) asserting: rewards native balance EQUALS tokenBuyAllowanceTotal exactly, rewards token balance covers all recognised HWA liabilities, module acquisition state never diverges from the core's, and core custody and native solvency still hold with rewards bound. `test/FWARewardsIntegrationBranches.t.sol` adds 10 deterministic tests that assert reachability rather than infer it.
findings.outcome: The protocol held. No custody or solvency violation was found across the newly reachable state space. The finding was about the evidence; the evidence is now real.
findings.residualRisk: The campaign uses a mock V3 router that mints at a fixed multiplier and ignores sqrtPriceLimitX96, so adapter price behaviour is still only covered by fork tests. Splitter remains outside this campaign.

findings.title: The audit manifest omitted 155 sources that are compiled into deployed bytecode, including the entire ERC-20 implementation of the HWA token
findings.scenario: `remappings.txt` resolves `solady/` to `vendor/fwa-reference-union/lib/solady/`, `@chainlink/contracts/` and `@uniswap/v4-core/` to sibling directories under the same vendor tree, and `fwa-rewards-reference/`, `fwa-hook-reference/`, `fwa-claim-reference/` and `fwa-splitter-reference/` to four FWA_ETHEREUM_REFERENCE subtrees. None of those directories was a manifest root. Solady supplies ERC20 (the deployed HWA token's whole token implementation), ERC721, Ownable, ReentrancyGuard, SafeTransferLib and FixedPointMathLib — every HyperEVM production contract links against it.
findings.impact: The SHA-256 anchor could not be used for what it exists to prove. A modified solady, or a swapped reference source, would ship with a fully matching manifest. The previous round recorded a related omission as Informational on the grounds that no unreviewed production surface existed; that assessment was wrong, because the omitted set includes deployed token code.
findings.evidence: Manifest verification at audit start: 285/285 hashes matched, 0 drift — while `Get-ChildItem vendor/fwa-reference-union` listed 65 unhashed .sol files including lib/solady/src/tokens/ERC20.sol. Regeneration with corrected roots produced 441 entries, +155 over the 286 in force at the time of the fix.
findings.fix: Added `vendor/fwa-reference-union`, `fork-test`, and the FWARewards / FWATokenHook / FWAClaim / Splitter reference source trees to the generator roots, and regenerated. Added a self-test that parses `remappings.txt`, resolves every target against the declared roots, and throws if any target falls outside — plus a direct assertion that solady is hashed.
regressionTests: scripts/TestReleaseScripts.ps1 — remapping-coverage assertion and solady-hashed assertion
findings.residualRisk: `contracts/lib/forge-std` remains unhashed. It is test-only tooling (StdInvariant) and never reaches deployed bytecode, so it is documented rather than anchored.

findings.title: The active Project X launch script accepted an unvalidated initial price, and Foundry's automatic root .env supplies a 1:1 testnet price plus a pre-confirmed tokenomics gate
findings.scenario: The prior round closed a High titled 'dangerous default initial price' by pointing at `.env.mainnet.example`, which ships `FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96` blank alongside `FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96_ECHO`, `MAINNET_FWA_MIN_INITIAL_FDV_HYPE_WEI` and `MAINNET_FWA_MAX_INITIAL_FDV_HYPE_WEI`. Those three variables were read by exactly one file — `script/InitializeNestMarket.s.sol`, the legacy Nest path — and under different names (`MAINNET_FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96_ECHO`). The active Project X launch script validated only `rawSqrtPrice > type(uint160).max`. Separately, a workspace-root `.env` exists and Foundry loads it automatically for every `forge script` invocation; it contains `FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96=79228162514264337593543950336` (exactly 2^96, price 1.0) and `FWA_TOKENOMICS_CONFIRMED=true`. An operator running the mainnet launch from a shell that did not import `.env.mainnet.local` would silently inherit both instead of failing closed on the deliberately blank template value.
findings.preconditions: Chain 999 launch executed without importing the mainnet env file into the process, or with the price field left unset in it. The workspace-root .env is present today.
findings.impact: HWA launches at 1 HWA = 1 HYPE, a fully diluted valuation of 1e9 HYPE, in a single atomic irreversible transaction that mints the whole 500M LP position into a locker with no withdrawal path. The market cannot be repriced afterwards.
findings.evidence: Grep confirms `FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96_ECHO` / `MAINNET_FWA_*_INITIAL_FDV_HYPE_WEI` appear only in `.env.mainnet.example` and `script/InitializeNestMarket.s.sol:54,64-65`. `.env` at the workspace root contains FWA_TOKENOMICS_CONFIRMED=true and FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96=2^96. `scripts/TestReleaseCandidate.ps1` refuses a root .env only under -MainnetMode; the deployment script itself carried no equivalent guard.
findings.fix: The active path now requires, on chain 999, `PROJECTX_MARKET_PRICE_CONFIRMED`, `PROJECTX_LP_LOCK_CONFIRMED`, a double-entry `FWA_INITIAL_SQRT_PRICE_X96_ECHO` match, and an FDV band checked after the token address is known. The echo requirement is also what defeats the implicit root .env: the stale testnet file defines no echo variable, so `vm.envUint` fails closed rather than launching.
findings.outcome: Fixed and covered. Note: this fix was applied by a concurrent remediation process during this audit, not by the auditor; it was reviewed and its regression test executed as part of the final gate.
findings.residualRisk: The FDV band is asserted after the factory deploys the token, so it relies on forge script simulating the whole run before broadcasting. That property holds for `forge script` but is not itself asserted anywhere. Operators should still remove the testnet .env from the workspace for the launch ceremony.

findings.title: The mainnet release gate exported the funded deployer private key into every npm child process
findings.scenario: Under `-MainnetMode` the gate calls `ImportEnvFile.ps1`, which sets every variable in `.env.mainnet.local` into the process environment with no allowlist — including `PRIVATE_KEY`. The gate then runs `npm ci`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run lint` and Playwright in that same environment. npm lifecycle scripts execute arbitrary third-party package code, which inherits the environment and can read the key.
findings.preconditions: Final mainnet gate run with a populated `.env.mainnet.local`.
findings.impact: Supply-chain exposure of the mainnet deployer key to the full transitive dependency tree of the frontend and indexer.
findings.evidence: ImportEnvFile.ps1:18 sets all keys unconditionally; TestReleaseCandidate.ps1 invokes npm for six steps after the import.
findings.fix: The gate now scrubs every variable matching PRIVATE_KEY / MNEMONIC / SECRET / PASSWORD / SEED_PHRASE / _TOKEN / API_KEY from the process environment immediately after the mainnet import and before the first child process, and records the scrubbed names in the report. The gate is broadcast-forbidden and never needs a signing key.
regressionTests: Report field `secretsScrubbedBeforeChildProcesses` is emitted by every run
findings.residualRisk: Operators who export secrets into their shell before invoking the gate are still exposed; the scrub only covers what the gate itself imports.

findings.title: -SkipFork and -SkipE2E produced a report with status 'passed' and skippedSteps 0
findings.lines: fork block, E2E block, report assembly
findings.scenario: The overall status is derived as failed / prepared / passed from the count of recorded skips. `-SkipFork` and `-SkipE2E` simply bypassed their blocks without calling `Add-GateSkip`, so a run that never executed the Project X mainnet fork simulation, the V3 testnet fork simulation or the 36 Playwright tests still reported `status: passed`, `skippedSteps: 0`, while `selection.minimumCounts` continued to advertise minimum counts that were never enforced.
findings.preconditions: Any gate invocation using either switch.
findings.impact: A materially weaker run is indistinguishable from a full one in the artefact the release relies on. This is the audited apparatus, not the product.
findings.evidence: The skip path existed only for the mainnet indexer build; the two switches had no else branch.
findings.fix: Both switches now record explicit skips with reasons, which forces status to 'prepared'.
regressionTests: Any -SkipFork/-SkipE2E run now emits skippedSteps > 0 and status 'prepared'

findings.title: Permissionless buyback() self-disables once spot leaves the static launch-derived price band, and the token has no other HYPE exit
findings.scenario: `launch()` derives `buybackSqrtPriceLimitX96` once, from the launch price, at 9535 bps in sqrt space — about +10% in price terms. `buyback()` passes that stored value verbatim to `exactInputSingle`. A Uniswap V3 pool requires the limit to be strictly beyond the current price in the swap direction and reverts with 'SPL' otherwise. Once HWA appreciates roughly 10% above its launch price — the expected outcome of a successful launch — every `buyback()` call reverts. Protocol HYPE continues to accrue to the token contract through its `receive()`, and `buyback()` is the only path by which HYPE can ever leave it: there is no rescue, sweep, withdraw or recover function on the token.
findings.preconditions: Public trading open and spot roughly 10% above the launch price. No attacker required; ordinary price appreciation is sufficient.
findings.impact: The advertised buyback loop — permissionless execution, 0.5% caller bounty, 40/40/20 routing to depositors, purchasers and burn — stops functioning, and accumulated protocol revenue is immobilised. Recovery requires the owner to call `setBuybackSqrtPriceLimitX96` and to keep re-setting it as price moves, turning a permissionless mechanism into one that depends on continual privileged intervention. If the owner key is lost or unavailable, the accrued HYPE is permanently stranded.
findings.evidence: FWATokenHyperEVM.sol:273-281 computes rawLimit as sqrtPriceX96 * 10000/9535 (HWA as token0) or * 9535/10000, then stores it; line 334 passes `buybackSqrtPriceLimitX96` unchanged into the adapter. Pattern search over FWATokenHyperEVM.sol for rescue / withdrawNative / sweep returns no matches. `test/mocks/MockHyperSwapV3.sol` ignores sqrtPriceLimitX96 entirely, so no in-repo test can observe this: the finding is invisible to the 136-test gate by construction.
findings.minimalFix: Either derive the price limit from current spot at buyback time with a bounded relative tolerance, or add an owner-independent path that lets a stalled buyback still route accrued HYPE. Both change slippage and MEV exposure.
findings.whyNotFixed: Every available remedy alters an economic parameter (the buyback slippage policy) or introduces a new administrative power. The audit mandate forbids changing economic parameters, tokenomics, delays, admin powers or product choices to close a finding without an explicit decision. This is therefore escalated, not patched.
findings.residualRisk: Until decided, the launch ships with a buyback mechanism that predictably stops working shortly after a successful launch, and with protocol revenue whose only exit depends on repeated owner action.

findings.title: Draw fairness depends on submitter liveness, not merely availability: an acquirer holds a free veto on an unfavourable round
findings.scenario: The target round's signature becomes public roughly 30 seconds after the request, while FWA's own word deadline is `selectionTimeoutBlocks` (360 blocks, about six minutes). Anyone can compute the derived word from the public signature as soon as the round publishes, because the derivation is a pure keccak over public inputs. Submission is permissionless, so an acquirer who dislikes the computed outcome simply does not submit, and — if no independent submitter does either — the request lapses and `_creditAcquisitionRefund` returns the escrowed acquisition fee.
findings.preconditions: Both protocol submitters down, lagging or censored for the six-minute window. The attacker still forfeits gas and the non-refunded randomness service fee.
findings.impact: During a submitter outage an acquirer gets a free option on the draw: fulfil favourable requests personally, let unfavourable ones expire for a refund. This contradicts DRAND_GELATO_RANDOMNESS_RUNBOOK.md section 1, which states the relayer is 'une dépendance de disponibilité, jamais une racine de confiance pour le résultat'.
findings.evidence: fulfillRandomness is externally callable by anyone with no allowlist; expireRequest is permissionless after REQUEST_EXPIRY_BLOCKS; FWA.sol:1571-1575 credits a refund when a Pending head passes its word deadline.
findings.minimalFix: No contract change closes this cleanly. Treat two independent, monitored submitters as a fairness control rather than an availability control, alert on any request older than a fraction of the word deadline, and correct the runbook claim.
findings.residualRisk: Bounded by submitter liveness and by the cost of the forfeited randomness service fee.

findings.title: requestRandomWords never fails closed against a target round whose beacon is already public
findings.scenario: The target round is computed as `roundAtOrAfter(block.timestamp + MIN_ROUND_DELAY_SECONDS)`. Unpredictability therefore rests entirely on chain time tracking wall-clock time within 30 seconds. HyperEVM publishes no bound on the divergence between block.timestamp and wall clock, and a proposer has some latitude over the timestamp it writes. If chain time lags by more than the configured margin, the signature for the selected round is already public when the acquisition is mined.
findings.preconditions: Sustained clock skew of 30 seconds or more, or proposer-level timestamp manipulation.
findings.impact: An acquirer could compute the selection outcome before committing, defeating the property that the requester cannot choose the winner.
findings.evidence: The 30-second floor is genuinely enforced by the contract (MIN_DELAY_SECONDS = 30, checked in the constructor), which correctly closes the previous round's F5-002. What remains unclosed is that nothing detects the skew condition itself.
findings.minimalFix: Cheap, non-economic hardening: revert if the target round is already proven in the registry, and require `targetRound > REGISTRY.latestProvenRound()`. Both are single SLOADs and can only trip in a state that should never occur in normal operation. Not applied here because its protective value depends on how continuously submitters feed the registry, which is an operational parameter that has not been fixed.
findings.residualRisk: Unquantified without a documented HyperEVM timestamp bound. This is the principal unproven assumption underpinning randomness fairness.

findings.title: The atomic launch is pre-emptively brickable at a fully predictable token address
findings.scenario: `DeployProjectXToken` deploys the launch factory in one transaction and calls `deployAndLaunch` in a second. After the first transaction the factory address is public, and the token is created by plain CREATE at nonce 1, so its address is deterministically derivable by anyone. `createAndInitializePoolIfNecessary` returns an existing pool untouched, and `launch()` then rejects it because the initialised price does not match. A third party who pre-creates and initialises the canonical 1% pool for the predicted token address makes `deployAndLaunch` revert.
findings.preconditions: Mempool observation of the factory deployment, or simply reading it after inclusion. Cost is one pool creation.
findings.impact: Denial of the launch. Recovery requires deploying a fresh factory, which the griefer can front-run again indefinitely. The residual danger is procedural: an operator under time pressure could instead adopt the attacker-chosen price, which no on-chain control prevents.
findings.evidence: Uniswap V3 pool creation does not call the token, so a pool can be created for an address that holds no code yet. The launch reverts atomically, so no partial state is created.
findings.minimalFix: Deploy the factory and call deployAndLaunch in a single transaction (constructor-driven launch), or derive the token address with CREATE2 from a secret salt.
findings.residualRisk: No funds at risk; availability and launch-price discipline only.

findings.title: Metadata route rate limiter is keyed on a spoofable header and backed by a map that is never evicted
findings.scenario: `rateLimited` keys its bucket on the first value of the client-supplied `x-forwarded-for` header, falling back to `x-real-ip`. Entries are inserted with `rateBuckets.set` and never deleted; a bucket is only reset when the same key returns after the window. An attacker sending requests with a fresh spoofed XFF value each time both bypasses the limit entirely and inserts an unbounded number of permanent map entries.
findings.preconditions: Reachable route. If the app sits behind a proxy that overwrites XFF, spoofing is prevented but unbounded growth from distinct real client IPs remains.
findings.impact: Rate limiting is ineffective, and the Node process grows without bound until it is killed.
findings.minimalFix: Trust only the proxy-assigned client address, and evict expired buckets (sweep on insert or use a bounded LRU).
findings.residualRisk: Availability only; no data exposure.

findings.title: rescueTokens is gated on a freely reversible owner boolean, so earned unclaimed HWA can be drained and normal operation resumed
findings.scenario: `rescueTokens` requires `IFWARewardsCore(core).canRescueRewards()`, which is `withdrawOnly && unsettledAcquisitionCount == 0`. `withdrawOnly` is a plain `onlyOwner` setBool with no timelock and no one-way latch — in deliberate contrast to REWARDS_REQUIRED_FOR_ACTIVATION, which the same function does latch one-way. `unsettledAcquisitionCount == 0` is the resting state. The owner can therefore set withdrawOnly, drain the module's entire token balance, and clear withdrawOnly in a single Safe multisend.
findings.preconditions: Owner Safe. No timelock is required anywhere in the deployment scripts, which check only that the owner address has code.
findings.impact: All depositor `tokenCredit`, all accrued active-listing emission and all unclaimed closed-epoch purchaser pots become unfunded while the on-chain liabilities remain recorded, so `withdrawTokens` reverts. `rescueTokens` also zeroes the emission rates permanently, retroactively shrinking already-closed epoch payouts, and `setEmission` cannot restore them once emission has started.
findings.minimalFix: Track a running total of settled credits and rescue only the surplus above it; make the withdraw-only gate one-way with a mandatory claim window.
findings.whyNotFixed: This is an administrative power. The mandate forbids altering admin powers to close a Medium without an explicit decision.
findings.residualRisk: Reduces to trust in the owner Safe and its signers. Should be covered by the timelock decision that is already an open launch gate.

findings.title: Splitter snapshot holders cannot discover their revenue in the UI because the snapshot collection is never indexed
findings.scenario: Holder revenue discovery resolves the caller's snapshot token IDs through indexer-provided ownership rows, but the indexer manifest is rendered only for gameplay collections; the Splitter snapshot collection is never added as a data source. Once the indexer is enabled the UI resolves an empty token set and reports nothing to claim.
findings.preconditions: Indexer enabled in the production manifest.
findings.impact: Snapshot holders see no claimable revenue and are unlikely to claim directly against the contract. `sweep()` transfers the entire remaining balance to the owner 365 days after `startRevenueClock`, so undiscovered holder revenue is ultimately routed away from holders. The contract-level claim path remains correct and open.
findings.minimalFix: Add the snapshot collection to the indexer manifest, or fall back to on-chain ownerOf enumeration bounded by MAX_TOKEN_ID when the indexer returns nothing.
findings.residualRisk: Financial harm to holders is real but requires the full 365 days to crystallise, and is fully preventable operationally.

findings.title: Purchaser and finalize windows are read live and can be retroactively compressed on already-allocated listings
findings.scenario: `settlementWindow` and `finalizeWindow` are read at settlement time rather than snapshotted at allocation, so an owner `setUint` retroactively changes the deadlines of listings that are already Allocated — including compressing the purchaser's 24-hour exclusive window to zero.
findings.impact: A purchaser's exclusive settlement right can be removed after the fact; an unbounded finalize window can make finalizeUnsettled unreachable.
findings.minimalFix: Snapshot both windows into the listing at allocation, and bound the setters.
findings.whyNotFixed: Changing a settlement time window is an economic and product parameter.
findings.residualRisk: Trust in the owner Safe.

findings.title: The drand attestation script verifies a decorative constant instead of the BN254 public key that defines the randomness source
findings.scenario: The attestation asserts the coordinator's DRAND_CHAIN_HASH, which is stored but never used in verification. The value that actually determines which beacon is trusted is the G2 public key returned by `DrandEvmnetRegistry.publicKey()`, and no attestation reads it.
findings.impact: A registry deployed with a substituted public key would pass the live 999 attestation the release gate depends on.
findings.minimalFix: Have the attestation read `publicKey()` and compare all four coordinates against the drand evmnet values, and assert the registry address the coordinator is bound to.
findings.residualRisk: Mitigated in this audit by direct verification against the live beacon (see the audit report), but not by any automated gate.

findings.title: On-chain position-discovery fallback is non-functional against the documented HyperEVM RPC: it requests 250,000-block log ranges against a 50-block cap
findings.scenario: LOG_DISCOVERY_CHUNK_BLOCKS is 250_000n (ViemProtocolClient.ts:63), while FWA_PARITY_MANIFEST.md:37 records that the official HyperEVM RPC caps eth_getLogs at 50 blocks. Each discovery request is 5000x over the documented cap, so the scan does not merely get throttled - it fails outright. Initially rated Medium on request volume; re-derived from source and raised to High on request width.
findings.preconditions: Indexer down or absent, which is exactly the fallback's purpose.
findings.impact: The documented indexer-independent exit path does not work against the documented RPC. Users cannot discover or exit positions when the indexer is down, which is exactly the emergency the fallback exists for.
findings.minimalFix: Not fixable by retuning the constant alone: at 50 blocks per request the scan is impractical. Requires a declared archival/log-capable RPC endpoint, plus checkpointing and partial results.
findings.residualRisk: Availability of the documented indexer-independent exit path.

findings.title: isPrivateAddress misclassifies NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-compatible and site-local IPv6 as public
findings.scenario: The IPv6 branch normalises only a leading `::ffff:` prefix and then matches `::1`, `::`, fc/fd and fe8-feb. Forms such as `::ffff:7f00:1`, `::127.0.0.1`, `64:ff9b::7f00:1` and `2002:7f00:1::` fall through and are treated as public.
findings.preconditions: An allowlisted host would have to resolve to such an address. The host allowlist, not this function, is the primary control.
findings.impact: Defence-in-depth gap only; not an exploitable bypass on its own.
findings.minimalFix: Normalise to a canonical form and classify against explicit CIDR ranges.
findings.residualRisk: Low while the allowlist is correctly configured and non-empty.

findings.title: The SSRF guard resolves the hostname and then reconnects by name, with no DNS pinning
findings.scenario: `assertPublicDestination` resolves the host and inspects the addresses, then discards them and calls `fetch(source)`, which re-resolves. A DNS entry that changes between the two lookups is not caught.
findings.preconditions: Attacker control over the DNS of a host that is already on the metadata allowlist.
findings.impact: Time-of-check/time-of-use gap, gated behind the allowlist.
findings.minimalFix: Connect to the validated IP with the Host header preserved, or use an agent with a pinned lookup.
findings.residualRisk: Low; requires compromising an allowlisted host's DNS.

findings.title: The published SSRF end-to-end test is vacuous, and the BN254 forgery test never reaches the pairing check
findings.scenario: The metadata spec's private-IP case is rejected by the host allowlist before the private-address guard runs, so the guard is untested. The drand forgery test flips a bit inside the signature's x coordinate, which fails the on-curve check in `isValidPointG1` and returns before `verifySingle`, so the pairing rejection path has no coverage.
findings.impact: Two security controls the release relies on have no executed negative test.
findings.minimalFix: Use an allowlisted host that resolves to a private address; forge a point that is on the curve but is not the correct signature.
findings.residualRisk: The controls were verified by inspection in this audit; they are simply not gate-enforced.

findings.title: BLS.isValidPointG2 and isValidPublicKey perform no G2 subgroup check
findings.scenario: Both helpers check field bounds and curve membership but not subgroup order. BN254 G2 has a large cofactor, so a curve point need not lie in the order-r subgroup.
findings.preconditions: Unreachable in this release: the only G2 point used is the hardcoded evmnet public key returned by DrandEvmnetRegistry.publicKey(), and neither helper is called on the mainnet path.
findings.impact: None today. Latent hazard if any future code accepts an attacker-supplied G2 point.
findings.minimalFix: Add a subgroup check before any use of these helpers on untrusted input, or delete the unused helpers.
findings.residualRisk: None while the public key stays a compile-time constant.

findings.title: Launch factory tick rounding is wrong at spacing-aligned ticks
findings.scenario: When HWA sorts as token0 the factory sets `tickLower = floorTick == currentTick ? currentTick : floorTick + spacing`. `getTickAtSqrtPrice` returns the floor tick, so an aligned currentTick does not imply the price sits exactly on the tick boundary; `launch()` then rejects the range because sqrtPriceX96 exceeds the price at tickLower.
findings.impact: A whole class of otherwise valid launch prices reverts. Launch-time only and retryable with a different price.
findings.minimalFix: Round up unless sqrtPriceX96 equals getSqrtPriceAtTick(floorTick) exactly.
findings.residualRisk: None beyond launch friction.

findings.title: Depositor emission accrued while no listing is active is permanently stranded, and buyback tokens routed to an empty epoch become an owner-only sweep
findings.scenario: `_advanceToken` advances `lastTokenAccrual` unconditionally but only credits `accTokenPerSqrt` when `sqrtBackingTotal != 0`, so emission for any interval with no active listing is skipped and the corresponding tokens stay in the contract. Separately, the depositor half of a buyback is burned when there are no active listings, but the purchaser half routed to an epoch that ends with zero settled acquisitions is neither burned nor distributed — it is recoverable only through the owner-only `sweepEmptyEpoch`, which is asymmetric with the depositor route and with the advertised 40/40/20 split.
findings.impact: No insolvency; both effects are conservative for claimants. They are economic leakage toward the owner and away from the documented split.
findings.minimalFix: Skip the clock when no listing is active; burn unclaimed empty-epoch purchaser amounts to mirror the depositor route.
findings.residualRisk: Quantifiable only once the activation timeline is fixed.

findings.title: Splitter wind-down and ownership edge cases
findings.scenario: Three separate small defects: (a) the 365-day holder claim window is not enforced relative to launch — nothing requires `startRevenueClock` to precede activation by any margin, so a window of one second is accepted; (b) `renounceOwnership` is reachable and would send `claimOwner` payouts to address(0) irreversibly while permanently disabling `sweep`; (c) deposits arriving after `sweep` has closed claims are silently accepted, unaccounted and emit no event.
findings.impact: Each is an operational foot-gun rather than an exploitable defect. Conservation itself is unaffected.
findings.minimalFix: Require a minimum clock lead time, override renounceOwnership to revert, and emit an event for post-close deposits.
findings.residualRisk: Operational.

findings.title: Manifest promotion and broadcast reporting remain self-asserted
findings.scenario: The five promotion confirmations are switch parameters the operator simply passes; no on-chain or artefact evidence is checked, and the `MAINNET_E2E_CONFIRMED` variable documented in the env template is read by no code. Separately, `broadcastPerformed` is derived from recorded steps, but `Invoke-GateStep` throws before recording a step when it detects `--broadcast`, so the field is structurally incapable of ever being true.
findings.impact: Report fidelity. The substantive no-broadcast guarantee still holds because `--broadcast` is actively rejected and `broadcastRequested` is genuinely measured.
findings.minimalFix: Have the promotion script verify acquisitionsEnabled, drand liveness and the gate artefact on chain; record rejected broadcast attempts as failed steps.
findings.residualRisk: None to funds; affects the trustworthiness of the release artefact.

findings.title: The audit anchor was regenerated and production files were modified during the audit window by a concurrent process
findings.scenario: At the start of this audit the manifest declared 285 files and verified 285/285 with zero drift. Partway through, it had been regenerated to 286 entries with a new timestamp, `script/DeployProjectXToken.s.sol` had changed, `test/utils/TestBase.sol` had grown, and a new `test/DeployProjectXTokenGuards.t.sol` had appeared. The changes correspond to a remediation of F5F-003 performed by a process other than this auditor. The same window also rewrote the previous round's reports, which the mandate requires to be preserved unmodified: release/FABLE5_SECURITY_AUDIT_2026-07-27.md grew from 16160 to 24747 bytes and release/fable5-security-findings-2026-07-27.json from 13012 to 21587 bytes. This auditor did not modify either file.
findings.impact: An audit anchor that is regenerated mid-audit cannot distinguish authorised remediation from tampering, and the previous round's audit trail is now weaker than when this audit began because its reports were edited in place rather than superseded. The findings and gate results in this report are stated against the final tree state, which was re-verified and re-anchored at the end.
findings.minimalFix: Freeze the tree for the duration of an audit, or require that every manifest regeneration record the reason and the prior root hash.
findings.residualRisk: Disclosed rather than mitigated. All conclusions here were re-derived against the final state.

findings.title: Assorted low-impact defects confirmed but not acted on
findings.scenario: Native HYPE force-sent to DrandBN254Coordinator is permanently unwithdrawable because withdrawNative caps at nativeSubscriptionBalance. `startRevenueClock` reverts with `AlreadyFrozen` when the split is not frozen, which will misdirect operators during the launch sequence. Unreachable vendored BLS helpers (expandMsg with n_bytes == 0, addG1Points, scalarMulG1Point) contain memory-safety defects. The 422 error response is cached publicly for five minutes. Indexer-supplied settlement outcome, acquisition price and crown status overwrite on-chain-derived values with no cross-check.

verifiedSound: SplitterHyperEVM conservation is exact: nftAllocation + ownerAllocation always equals msg.value, per-token payout is bounded by floor(nftAllocated / SNAPSHOT_SUPPLY), rounding residue is retained by the contract, duplicate token IDs in one claim array are idempotent, and forceSafeTransferETH prevents a reverting recipient from griefing others.

FWARewardsHyperEVM native conservation is exact and is now proven by an equality invariant: the module has no receive or fallback, so HYPE can only enter through settleAcquisition (msg.value == tokenSlice) or buyFor (spent in the same call).

drand evmnet constants verified first-hand against the live beacon: chain hash 04f1e906..ec8c3, period 3, genesis 1727521075 and scheme bls-bn254-unchained-on-g1 all match; the repository fixture signature for round 19159982 is a genuine live drand signature; sha256(signature) reproduces the published randomness exactly.

The pinned G2 public key is byte-identical to drand's published serialisation, and the coordinate order passed to the pairing precompile (x[1], x[0], y[1], y[0]) reconstructs that serialisation exactly.

randomness = sha256(signature) is not grindable: isValidPointG1 explicitly rejects x >= N or y >= N, so non-canonical encodings of a valid point cannot produce an alternative hash. BN254 G1 has cofactor 1, so on-curve implies in-subgroup, and the point at infinity (0,0) fails the curve equation.
MIN_DELAY_SECONDS = 30 is a contract constant enforced in the constructor, not merely a deployment configuration value. The previous round's F5-002 is genuinely closed at the contract level.

No exploitable SSRF bypass was found. The metadata route uses a strict host allowlist rather than a denylist, rejects userinfo, sets redirect to 'error', caps the decompressed response stream at 512 KB, applies a 5-second timeout, permits no active SVG or HTML image types, validates IPFS path segments against traversal, and fails closed to the IPFS gateway alone when the allowlist is empty.
No chain-999 transaction has ever been broadcast from this workspace: the broadcast directory contains chain 998 only.

PrepareMainnetOwnerActions performs genuine on-chain attestation: chain 999, deployed bytecode at every address, a contract Safe owner shared by all modules, acquisitions closed, withdraw-only clear, empty pool, emission not started, external buys closed, and executable false unless RPC-validated.
